feeds.title: Stuttering Society
feeds.description: Stuttering Society is the realization of a long-held dream to create an online platform that truly embraces the stuttering community and their needs. As well as empowering and connecting people who stutter, we encourage meaningful conversations about issues related to communication disorders and strive to find new solutions to help those who stutter in different aspects of their lives.

feeds.title: McGuire Programme News Blog
feeds.description: We provide intensive 3 to 4-day courses and extensive follow-up support throughout the world to help people who stutter overcome this affliction and become good speakers. Our program has evolved and is constantly evolving to where it is becoming more and more effective for people who stutter and want to do something positive about it.

feeds.title: Redefining Stammering Blog
feeds.description: I am Sam. I am a speech and language therapist with over 25 years experience of working with people who stammer and their families in the public, private, education, and voluntary sectors. I have a particular interest in disability studies, stammering activism, and what stammering can teach us about ourselves and the world

feeds.title: Stuttering Therapy Resources Blog
feeds.description: Our mission is to help speech-language pathologists (SLPs) help people who stutter by offering practical, affordable resources that are grounded in the lived experience of people who stutter, the clinical experience of stuttering specialists, and current scientific research evidence.

feeds.title: Make Room For The Stuttering
feeds.description: Make Room For The Stuttering was created by me, Pamela A Mertz after realizing that I have a story to tell. I was a covert stutterer for many years and was afraid to stutter publicly. Since opening up about my stuttering, my world has opened up, profoundly and deeply. I feel it is my responsibility to share my journey with others whose lives have been touched by stuttering.

feeds.title: Stuttering Foundation Blog
feeds.description: We provide free online resources, services, and support to those who stutter and their families, as well as support for research into the causes of stuttering. The Stuttering Foundation offers continuing education courses for ASHA CEUs online. Developed and led by world-renowned experts, these courses are offered at low cost to speech-language pathologists (SLPs) worldwide.

feeds.title: The Genetics of Stuttering Study Blog
feeds.description: Find out more about our research study, information on stuttering, the latest stuttering research, and other useful resources! The study aims to pinpoint the genes that predispose individuals to stutter. This could revolutionize future research into the causes, and biology of stuttering.

feeds.title: Cadence Speech Blog
feeds.description: At Cadence Speech Therapy, our passion is to help clients achieve functional fluency to confidently communicate in all areas of their lives. We achieve this by providing high-quality, comprehensive, client-centered evaluations and therapy. We specialize in stuttering therapy for children, teens, and adults, as well as provide expert services for speech sound disorders.

feeds.title: West Coast Stuttering Center Blog
feeds.description: West Coast Stuttering Center was founded by me, Bailey Levis, M.S., CCC-SLP, a licensed Speech-Language Pathologist and person who stutters. His mission is to provide holistic and integrative speech therapy to support you or your child in meeting this need with dignity and confidence. From childhood through adulthood, I focus on helping individuals engage in communication without fear or anxiety. Personalized speech therapy will guide you to feel understood and to freely engage with the world around you.

feeds.title: HCRI Stuttering Therapy Blog
feeds.description: HCRI was founded by Ronald L. Webster, Ph.D. in 1972 to investigate stuttering with scientific methods and new treatment approaches. Under Dr. Webster´s direction, Virginia-based HCRI, a nonprofit organization, has become an international leader in stuttering research and the development of innovative, scientifically based therapy approaches.

feeds.title: Hello I Stutter
feeds.description: My name is Rehan Nasir, and I'm 42, an American engineer working in Lancaster, PA, USA. I have been stuttering since I was 7. I'm divorced and now remarried - we have five kids! Before moving back home to Lancaster, we lived in Indianapolis for two years. My objective for this site is to have a conversation about stuttering on a regular basis. It's taken me this long to get online with this because I'm a closet stutterer - that is, I don't want people to know that I stutter.

feeds.title: Power Stuttering Therapy Blog
feeds.description: Mark Power, BCS-F has been a Board Certified Stuttering Specialist in Fluency for 20 years. Mark was part of the original, Initial Cadre of the American Speech-Language and Hearing Association that developed Specialty Recognition for Stuttering Therapy. These specialists gathered to solve the problem of the lack of training in stuttering, which allows general speech pathologists to treat stutterers without advanced training.

feeds.title: Every Waking Moment Blog
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Chris. I am a person who stutters, or a stutterer, who writes and speaks about the lived experience of stuttering. While I write mostly about my journey through and into self-acceptance, my story is your story whether you stutter or not. I hope to use words written and spoken to help change how stuttering is lived, confronted, and perceived in a world in which its viewed as a disability, disorder, and an impediment.

feeds.title: Stamurai Blog
feeds.description: Stamurai is a Mobile app to help you learn and practice speech therapy exercises for stuttering. Get the most up-to-date information on stuttering, therapy techniques, tips on how to stop stuttering, and more.

feeds.title: Free From Stutter Blog
feeds.description: My name is Andrey Denisenko. I'm passionate about helping people who stutter get free from stuttering. We can't change the genes, and we can't change the way we're wired, but we can drastically change the way we feel about speaking interaction. We can be truly present and enjoy it. We can drastically change the way we feel about speaking. We can be open, active, and positive about speaking interaction and ourselves.
